name: readme-format-feature-coverage
body:
source: v0.10.0 release defect — README.md was not updated for the new user-facing template-feature set. requirements.requirement.readme-presentation required the README as the polished front page retaining all technical content, but nothing required it to document the newly added user-facing format features. README.md line 319–320 still said ""the v1 template helper set stays exactly `media`"" and its ""`.deck` and `.slide` context"" section (line ~317) still said ""two reserved, read-only names"". The v0.10.0 format actually provides four layout helpers (`media`, `section`, `dict`, `list` — template-language, section-helper, dict-list-helpers) and five reserved contexts (`deck`, `slide`, `item`, `raw`, `data` — template-context, item-context, raw-source-context, section-data-context), with `deck`/`slide`/`item`/`raw`/`data` reserved top-level names. The README lagged the format while the AGENTS.md deck guide (agent-authoring) had been kept current.

inconsistency: README.md's format documentation and the format as specified diverge — the human-facing front page documents a subset (one helper, two contexts) of what template-language and the context requirements provide (four helpers, five contexts). No requirement made README documentation of user-facing format features a condition of shipping them.

resolution [autonomous]: do NOT add a new requirement — the concern already belongs to requirements.requirement.readme-presentation. Strengthen that requirement with (1) a clause that the README documents the current user-facing template-format features — the layout helper set (`media`, `section`, `dict`, `list`) and the reserved contexts (`.deck`, `.slide`, `.item`, `.raw`, `.data`) and reserved names — and that a user-facing format feature is not shipped until the README documents it (the README is the human counterpart of the AGENTS.md deck guide), and (2) a matching AC requiring the README's helper set and reserved-context list to match the format (no smaller set, no fewer contexts). The README.md edit itself is the plan/implementation's job, not this reconciliation's.
